resources.string: Runs while a conversation is active.
Start live mode, put the phone down and just talk. After every answer the app listens again by itself. Saying “stop” ends the conversation without touching anything.

The download is the only moment the app goes online, and it resumes by itself after a dropout. Models with a licence also need an access token; “Find more” only lists those without one.
Hugging Face token (only needed for Gemma)

Faster, but not stable on every device
Changes to the model or to generation take effect from the next turn; the model is reloaded then. LiteRT-LM handles the chat template and the conversation history itself.
There is no language model on the device yet. Without one only a placeholder answers.
The download happens once and needs a connection. Everything runs offline afterwards. Wi-Fi is a good idea.
If the connection drops, it continues by itself after %1$d seconds - at the same place. Pausing loses nothing either.
Hugging Face only releases %1$s once you have accepted the licence and stored an access token.
1. Open the model page and accept the licence. 2. Create a read access token on huggingface.co under Settings. 3. Enter the token in the settings below.
Google\'s small language model. Fluent on a phone and a good fit for a spoken conversation.
Very small and fast, but thin on substance. Good for testing the loop on weak hardware.
Bigger and slower, but answers with more substance. Apache licence, downloads without a token.
Found on Hugging Face, downloads without accepting a licence.

You are a spoken assistant running entirely offline on a phone. Answer briefly, in full sentences, and in the language the user speaks. Two or three sentences are almost always enough. No bullet points, no headings, no markdown - everything is read aloud.
I did not catch that. Say it again if you like.

I understood: %1$s. But I am only the placeholder. Load a model file in the settings and I will answer properly.
